title: Compile elevation and grade-separated road structures
acceptance: an authoritative and distributable NYC-compatible elevation/DEM source is selected, pinned, documented, and ingested by the compiler
road elevations/grades are generated in meters and remain continuous enough for the vehicle to traverse ordinary slopes without artificial steps at tile or segment boundaries
OSM bridge, tunnel, layer, ramp, and related topology semantics are combined with elevation so grade-separated crossings do not become false flat intersections
compiler fixtures cover at least one bridge/viaduct, one tunnel or below-grade segment, and one multi-level highway/ramp case representative of NYC complexity
diagnostics identify unresolved or contradictory vertical topology instead of silently flattening it
verify: python3 -m pytest tools/map_compiler/tests -k 'elevation or bridge or tunnel or grade'
verification: PR #11 final production-only head passed the declared T010 elevation/bridge/tunnel/grade pytest selection, the full map-compiler suite, hosted npm run check (TypeScript, unit tests, production build), project health, lint/types/schemas, and both Ubuntu and Windows Roach coordination/state validation. Temporary Chromium verification run 33451655491 and artifact 9779977412 loaded the real built game at Roadbed with stable 4/4 wheel contacts, exercised normal R recovery back to Roadbed with 4/4 contacts, and recorded no browser/page errors. The temporary browser workflow was removed before merge.

evidence.work: Pinned and ingested the 2017 NYC LiDAR bare-earth DEM; added metric schema-v2 elevation output, CSCL/OSM vertical topology resolution, continuous bridge/tunnel/ramp profiles, explicit topology diagnostics, elevated Roadbed rendering/collision, schema-v2 flat-support exclusion, elevation-aware spawn/reset/fall recovery, deterministic compiler/runtime tests, and source/uncertainty documentation. Merged through PR #11; browser artifact 9779977412 verified the real browser runtime and safe reset path.
